CV of Failures

Entering a PhD program at 31 from an ‘alt music’/DIY background means constantly navigating the gap between institutional validation and the work itself, especially as someone who aims to nurture a decolonial position in their work. This document exists to normalize rejection as part of my development and remind myself that persistence often matters more than any single outcome.

Degree Program Near-Misses

  • Ph.D. Texts & Technology, University of Central Florida , 2025.
    • Waitlisted for admission; received late admission without funding.

Conference Rejections

  • “Critical Making’s Debts and Extensions: Engaging Decolonial Epistemologies as Predicate,” Global Digital Humanities Symposium 2026, Michigan State University, 13-17 April 2026.

    • “While this proposal provides a clear indication of the author’s knowledge of theory with respect to critical making, there is a lot of jargon used and I’m not entirely clear on the relationship between what the author is arguing and specific practice in the field of digital humanities. This proposal raises an interesting set of questions and ethical considerations, to be sure, but it would be much stronger if it cited and addressed specific DH projects. “

Publication Rejections

  • The Cypress Dome, April 2021.
    • Creative writing piece about a spring break slasher movie a la the nouveau roman that would eventually become Like a Mountain of Sleep years later.

Position Rejections

  • Associate Editor. The Pegasus Review: UCF Undergraduate Research Journal.May 2021
    • Rejected on first application. Hired the following year—went on to co-lead workshops, edit essays for publication, and help select future candidates.

Developing Skills

  • Grant writing
  • Navigating institutional timelines while maintaining creative practice
